---
title: "Cleaning supermarket data with tidyr"
author: "Nikhil"
date: "2024-04-23"
categories: [R, application]
---
In this case study we got a supermarket dataset where every row is one customer and every cell is one item they scanned at the till. Each scan looks like "10 24 1.09", which is the department, the time and the price all squeezed together. To analyse it we first need to tidy it up.  

[Code on Github](https://github.com/nikh123/ELABII)

# *Give the columns names*  

The raw file has no headers, so I named the columns `Item_1`, `Item_2`, … and added a `Customer_ID` for each row.
```
library(tidyverse)
data <- read.csv("supermarket.csv")
sampled_data <- data[1:50, ]

colnames(sampled_data) <- paste0("Item_", 1:ncol(sampled_data))

sampled_data <- mutate(Customer_ID = row_number(), sampled_data)
```

# *From wide to long*  

With `pivot_longer` every scan gets its own row, then the empty cells are removed.
```
sampled_data <- sampled_data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Item"),
               names_to = "Item",
               values_to = "Scan") %>%
  arrange(Customer_ID) %>%
  group_by(Customer_ID) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Scan) & Scan != "")
```

# *Split the scan*  

Finally `substring` splits the scan into three proper columns that we can use for the analysis.
```
sampled_data <- sampled_data %>%
  mutate(Department = substring(Scan, 1, 3),
         Time = as.integer(substring(Scan, 4, 6)),
         Price = as.numeric(substring(Scan, 7)))
```
Now the data has one row per item with the customer, department, time and price, which makes it easy to group, summarise and plot.
